background_notes.fact: For the displayed map j(t)=(x0,t), any countable delta-cover (V_i) of F pulls back to a countable delta-cover W_i={t in I:j(t) in V_i} of I, with diam(W_i)<=diam(V_i). For every fixed s>0, this implies H^s_delta(I)<=H^s_delta(F), and hence H^s(I)<=H^s(F).

grounds.reason: The Euclidean product metric gives the displayed distance equality, including n=0.
I is the subset [0,1] of R.
Every (x0,t) with t in I belongs to F.
Diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances, with empty diameter zero.
Contents are infima of countable-cover costs and measure is the supremum over positive scales.
j, an arbitrary positive scale, and an arbitrary countable delta-cover are explicitly constructed or quantified.

background_notes.justification: Coverage follows pointwise from j(I) subset F. For t,u in W_i, the distance equality bounds |t-u| by diam(V_i), so taking the pairwise supremum gives the diameter inequality; empty W_i also satisfy it. The nonnegative power function r↦r^s is increasing for s>0, so termwise costs and then countable nonnegative sums compare (a countable nonnegative sum is the supremum of its finite subsums). Thus H^s_delta(I) is at most every admissible cost for F, and hence at most their infimum; an empty target-cover family gives the same inequality against infinity. Taking supremums over the same positive scales preserves the inequality. This uses the actual cover proof in S002, without an imported dimension monotonicity theorem. Although only 0<s<1 is needed, the calculation is valid for every fixed s>0.

background_notes.fact: If d is an extended nonnegative real and d>=s for every real 0<s<1, then d>=1.

grounds.reason: F001 gives infinite H^s(F) for every 0<s<1 under L1.
For F in Eucl(n+1), infinite H^s(F) implies dim_H(F)>=s.
dim_H(F) is an extended nonnegative real.

background_notes.justification: If d<1 then d is finite, with real representative r satisfying 0<=r<1. The real s=(r+1)/2 satisfies 0<s<1 and r<s, contradicting d>=s. This verifies the 'letting s increase to 1' step by order alone.
